issue.title: gateway: Qoder's per-model queue 503 rests the whole account, so sibling models are refused without asking upstream
issue.body:
# gateway: Qoder's per-model queue 503 rests the whole account, so sibling models are refused without asking upstream

## Summary

A provider that answers a **per-model** rate/queue refusal with a 5xx (Qoder's `503 ... queued the request for <model>`), instead of a 429, is classified as `failOther` and rests the **whole account** (`restKey()`). Sibling models that the same account can still serve are rested with it, and with more than one account the group ends up failover-ing between accounts on the one model that is out, each resting its account.

This is the same shape of problem as #3039 (a relay's model-scoped 429 resting the whole key) and WorkBuddy's "switch to other models" (handled in `restAfterMarked`), but it arrives on a **different branch**: `failOther` rather than `failQuota`/`failRate`.

## The refusal

Qoder answers a congested free model with:

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable

Qoder: Qoder queued the request for <model> (this plan's queue: p3); try again in 30s
```

The body names exactly one model, and the queue is that plan's queue for that model. The account's other models are not in it and still answer.

## Where it lands

`internal/gateway/routing.go`, `failure(status, body)`:

- `proxyDown` (L351) — no
- `Verification` on 401/403 (L354) — no
- `restrictedSaid` (L360) — no
- `overflowed` (L362) — no
- `status == 402` (L366, L373) — no
- `status == 429` (L375, L381, L385) — no
- `status >= 500 && quotaCodes.Match(body)` (L383) — **no**: `quotaCodes` is `limit reached\|\d{10}\b|usage_limit_reached|RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, and the body says "queued the request"

→ falls through to `return failOther` (L388).

`restAfterMarked`, the `default:` branch (L898–944):

```go
counted := c.restKey()
if unserved {                     // only a model the plan does not serve
    counted = c.restID()
}
```

`unserved` requires `modelRefused(status, body) || codeAssistModelMissing(...)`, neither of which matches a queue refusal. So `counted = c.restKey()`: the **account** rests, on the whole-account backoff ladder (`min(fallbackCooldown<<min(n-1,10), RestCap)`, 1 → 2 → 4 … minutes).

## Why the model-scoping that exists does not catch it

`restAfterMarked` already narrows the rest to the model in four cases (L962–989):

| condition | why it does not apply here |
|---|---|
| `why == failRate && isOpenRouterFree() && sharedPool` | not OpenRouter |
| `pooled \|\| unserved \|\| modelBackoff \|\| why == failQuota && resetsWhen && otherModels` | **requires `failQuota`**; this is `failOther` |
| `why == failQuota && clineModelLimited` | requires `failQuota` |
| `(why == failCredit \|\| why == failQuota) && PaidBesideFree` | requires quota/credit |

Every narrowing branch keys on `failQuota`, `failCredit` or `failRate`; none covers `failOther`, and none matches a body that merely names the model being queued.

`rateRest`'s comment (L1025–1033) shows the same gap from the other side: it notes WorkBuddy's free model being refused repeatedly while the account still had credits, and fixes the **length** of the rest (doubling backoff), but not its **scope** — the account still rests whole.

## Effect

- One model out → every model of that account rests until the ladder ends.
- Two accounts, one model out → each rests its account, and the group alternates accounts on a model that is out for both, paying a whole-account rest each time.
- `magpie accounts` / the Providers page report the account as out although its other models answer upstream.

## Suggestion

Narrow the rest to the model when the refusal names it, on whichever branch it arrives:

- in `failure()`, a 5xx (and a 429) whose body names the model being asked — the way `otherModels` / `modelRefused` already key on wording — could be its own reason, or
- in `restAfterMarked`'s `default:` branch, treat a body naming `c.model` (as `Qoder queued the request for <model>` does) as `unserved`-like for the purpose of the rest key, so `counted = c.restID()`.

Either way the account's siblings keep going upstream, and only the model whose queue refused is benched — matching what the existing WorkBuddy / Cline / OpenRouter branches already do.

## Notes

- Same branch (`failOther`) is reached for any vendor that answers a per-model queue/congestion with a 5xx instead of a 429, so the fix is not Qoder-specific.
- Reported from the Windows desktop build, gateway `v0.1.1307`; the code paths above are read at `origin/main` (`7dd965ed`).

comments.body:
修了（按你建议的第二种：在 `restAfterMarked` 的 default 分支收窄），在分支 [skygunner:fix/queue-model-rest](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/queue-model-rest)（commit 1b9f089，基于 main 87d703c5）。README 说本仓库不开 PR，放在这里供取用。

改动：

- `fallback.go` 新增 `queuedWords`（`(?i)queued the request for`，按措辞不按厂商——任何以 5xx 回已把请求排进该模型队列的都算，与你说的非 Qoder 特判一致）。
- `restAfterMarked`：`why == failOther && status >= 500` 且命中间隔词时 `queued` 为真——失败计数走 `restID`（自己的梯子）、休息 key 走 `restID`（账号的其他模型照常问）；不再给账号计数。普通 5xx 仍整账号歇。
- gateway-routing.md 的对应段落补了一句。

**验证**（`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8`、`umask 022`；commit body 有完整记录）

- 新增 `TestQueuedModelRestsAlone`：改动前红——你引的 503 原文让 `qoder@u@x.com`（整账号）歇下；改动后绿——模型按 `restID` 单独歇、同账号 glm-5.3 不歇、不带队列措辞的普通 503 仍歇整账号。
- `TestRest*`、`TestModelLadder*`、`TestCodeAssistMissingModelRestsTheModel`、`TestRemoteMagpie*` 全绿；三平台 vet/build 通过；全量 67 ok（除 #2207、#3280 两个 main 既有红外无新增）。
- 没有对真实 Qoder 上游试过；refusal 字节取自你的 issue。"try again in 30s" 没有读成重试时间——梯子照旧，如果你想让它按 vendor 给的时间歇，那是另一小步（`resetsInWords` 家族），可以加。

分支跟着 main 走了一步：上游把 `restAfterMarked` 从 fallback.go 挪进了 routing.go（#3274 的 refusal 整理和新的 slow-start 休息），[skygunner:fix/queue-model-rest](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/queue-model-rest) 已 rebase 到当前 main be002aca（commit 50eac57f），语义不变——queued 5xx 仍按 `restID` 只歇该模型、不计账号。internal/gateway 全包在新 main 上重跑通过（唯一红是 #3280 的 /bin/sh 既有问题，main 即红）。

The gap is real on current main, and one design decision needs the maintainer before a patch lands — so this is a judgment, not a patch.

The residual gap
---

Current main (`759b4d1d7`) still has no reading for a 5xx that says the *model's* queue took the request ("Qoder queued the request for <model> (this plan's queue: p3); try again in 30s"): it is not in `quotaCodes`, not 429, not `vendorOverloaded` — so it falls to `failOther` and `restAfterMarked`'s default branch rests the whole account (`restKey`), exactly as the report says. A sibling model the same account still serves is refused without being asked, and a two-account group fails over between accounts, paying a whole-account rest each time.

What changed under it since the report
---

Main has since grown a neighboring mechanism in the same branch: `vendorOverloaded` (a 529, or a 5xx whose words say "overloaded") rests nobody at the account — `!unserved && c.model != ""` reads it as the vendor's moment, not the account's fault. The Qoder wording does not match it ("queued", not "overloaded"), so the shape now has two neighbors:

| word family | branch | what rests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "overloaded" / 529 | `vendorOverloaded` | nobody (any account would have met it alike) |
| "queued the request for <model>" | nothing — falls to default | the whole account (the report's bug) |
| per-model quota/credit/rate | `modelCooledDown` (#3039) | that model alone, its own ladder |

Two ways to close it, for the maintainer's call:

- **A (the branch's way):** a `queuedWords` reading — a 5xx saying the request was queued *for the model it names* is that model's own congestion: rest that model alone (`restID`, its own backoff), the account's other models still served. @skygunner's branch `fix/queue-model-rest` (`50eac57f`, rebased onto `be002aca`) implements exactly this, with `TestQueuedModelRestsAlone` (red before, green after) and a wording-based match, so any vendor answering its model's queue with a 5xx benefits. Its `restAfterMarked` has since moved and grown (`zcodeTrialBlocked`, `vendorOverloaded`, slow-start rests), so the branch needs one more rebase; the hunks sit beside the new `overloaded` line and no longer apply as is.
- **B (the narrower reading):** "queued the request for" is the vendor saying it *did not start the turn* — closer to `vendorOverloaded`'s "nobody rests, ask again" than to a model-scoped rest. The report's own "try again in 30s" then argues only for honoring the named time (the `resetsInWords` family), not a backoff ladder.

A stands closer to the report's ask (siblings keep serving); B is the smaller semantic step from what main already does for overloads. The design call — model-scoped rest vs. nobody-rests — belongs to the maintainer.

Not verified: a real Qoder upstream (the refusal bytes are from the report); the branch's own tests were not re-run here since its base has drifted.

AI use: analysis performed with AI assistance; all code reads above were run locally at `759b4d1d7`.

Thanks @liubai0106 for the report and @skygunner for the fix branch and the rebase.

issue.title: gateway: SophNet's model-scoped 429 ("Model tpm limit exceeded") rests the whole key, greying out every model on it

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

When a SophNet model answers a **model-scoped** 429, magpie rests the **whole API key**, so every sibling model on that key is greyed out on the Routing page (`rate limited · back in 59 s`) and gets a local 429 without the request ever reaching upstream.

This is the same shape as #3039 (a relay's `for model <X>` 429) and #3213 (Qoder's per-model 503), but it arrives with **different wording** that none of the existing matchers catch:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests

{"error":{"message":"SophNet: Model tpm limit exceeded. Please try again later."}}
```

## Evidence from the gateway trace

A group `group/deepseek-v4-flash` with three members on one SophNet key. The first member gets the 429 above, and `/api/gateway/trace` records the rest against the **key**:

```json
{
  "id": "sophnet",
  "model": "DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017",
  "status": 429,
  "fail": "rate",
  "error": "SophNet: Model tpm limit exceeded. Please try again later.",
  "rest": {
    "why": "rate",
    "status": 429,
    "until": "2026-10-25T22:54:24Z",
    "by": "cooldown",
    "failures": 1,
    "key": "sophnet@api key …pncw"      // ← whole key, not restID()
  }
}
```

The next two members were tried within ~1s and each got its own 429, after which all three rows showed `rate limited · back in 59 s`. The same happens for every other model on that key.

## Expected

Recognise `Model <name> limit exceeded` (and similar "the limit is for this model" phrasing) as a **model-scoped** refusal and call `c.restID()` instead of `c.restKey()`, like `otherModels` does for `switch to other models` in #3039.

The distinction matters here: SophNet's console exposes per-model TPM/RPM (e.g. 600k TPM, 120 RPM per model), so a `Model tpm limit exceeded` does not necessarily mean the key's whole quota is gone. If the sibling models are in fact on a shared pool, letting the request go upstream and answer its own 429 is still more truthful than pre-emptively refusing it locally with another model's error text.

## Trade-off worth considering

I understand the conservative choice (don't hammer a key that just 429'd). A middle ground could be: rest the model immediately, but for siblings only apply a short "probe" cooldown (or none), and rest the whole key only if a second distinct model on the same key also 429s.

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.1543, Linux (workstation), custom SophNet plugin provider (`@ai-sdk/openai` / `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, per-model `limit.context` / `limit.output`)
- Three channels under one SophNet API key: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, `-global`, `DeepSeek-Flash-1017`, routed `order`/`auto`
- Reproduced by sending concurrent requests through the group until SophNet answers `Model tpm limit exceeded`

## Workaround

Routing page → `Try now` on the key lifts the rest immediately (as #3039 notes); restarting magpie also clears it.

issue.title: qoder: make the queue wait budget configurable (plugin waits 4 min, Qoder's own client waits up to 1 hour)

repository.name: plugins
repository.description: Community-maintained OpenCode provider plugins for coding-plan subscriptions (work in OpenCode and magpie)

issue.body:
## Summary

When a Qoder model is queued (error code `10605`, e.g. `queueType: p3`), the Qoder plugin polls the queue status and waits at most **4 minutes**, then returns `503 + Retry-After`. Qoder's own client waits up to **1 hour** for the same queue.

With Codex, this produces a visible "stop, then resume": Codex receives the 503 at the 4-minute boundary and retries, even though Qoder itself would have continued waiting.

This is not the group retry storm fixed in yetone/magpie#5346. With a single Qoder provider and no fallback, the remaining gap is the hard-coded `QUEUE.budget`.

## Environment

- Magpie: 0.1.3184 (macOS)
- Qoder plugin: 0.2.61
- Client: Codex Desktop 0.166.0-alpha.6
- Model: `qoder/smodel` (Sonus)
- Qoder provider: single account, no fallback / routing group

## What happens

1. Codex sends a request to `qoder/smodel` through Magpie.
2. Qoder answers with `10605`: `isQueued: true`, `retryAfterSeconds: 30`, `queueType: p3`.
3. The plugin polls `/api/v2/service/ask/queue/status` and sends nothing to Codex while waiting.
4. At 4 minutes the plugin gives up and returns `503`.
5. Codex retries. The retry may answer quickly, so the user sees a pause followed by a restart.

## Evidence

Local Magpie log:

```text
2026/11/06 00:29:50 gateway: codex's call to qoder/smodel on qoder failed:
503 after 4m9.596s: Qoder: Qoder queued the request for smodel
(this plan's queue: p3); try again in 30s
```

Corresponding Codex session:

- Turn 1: time to first token `193.4s`, completed in `194.5s`
- Turn 2: time to first token `270.6s`, completed in `271.1s`
- The `503` landed in turn 2 after the 4-minute budget; the retry produced the first token about 20 seconds later

Qoder CLI logs on the same machine also show real queue answers with `10605`, for example `queueCount: 284 / 666 / 1558 / 2092`, all on `queueType: p3`.

## Code / docs

`packages/qoder/index.mjs`:

```js
const QUEUE = {
  budget: 4 * 60 * 1000, // the longest a request is held, its first answer's wait included
  ...
}
```

`packages/qoder/README.md` already documents the difference:

> Qoder's client waits up to an hour; the plugin waits at most 4 minutes from the request's start, since nothing reaches the agent meanwhile (magpie keeps a stream's agent alive with comments for 5 minutes of silence).

So the 4-minute cap appears intentional. The request is to make it configurable, or to align it with Qoder's own client behavior for clients that can tolerate a longer first-token wait.

## Why this matters

- Waiting in a vendor queue is not a transient upstream failure. Returning 503 and retrying can re-queue the same request and add another wait.
- The user-visible result is exactly what Qoder's own client avoids: a long silence, a cancellation, then a second request.
- A positive Qoder balance does not guarantee a queue slot; paid models can still sit in `p3`.
- Codex can tolerate long first-token waits if the stream stays alive, but the plugin currently gives up before Codex's own timeout would.

## Proposal

1. Make the Qoder queue budget configurable, for example:
   - `MAGPIE_QODER_QUEUE_BUDGET_MS`, or
   - a Qoder provider setting such as `queueBudgetMs`
2. Keep the current 4-minute default if that is the safe default for most clients, but allow a longer value up to Qoder's own client behavior (1 hour).
3. Document the interaction with Magpie's 5-minute stream keepalive and Codex's SSE idle timeout. If the budget is raised above ~5 minutes, the plugin/gateway should send keepalive comments or the client timeout must be raised too.
4. When the budget expires, return a clear message that the request was queued, not a generic upstream failure; include the queue type and the suggested retry delay.

## Related

- magpie-community/plugins#427 — maintainer confirms Qoder queues and the 4-minute agent wait
- yetone/magpie#5346 — one request retried 25x on 429/queued answers; fixed in 0.1.3087 by not re-asking the group and letting the last candidate wait in Qoder's queue
- yetone/magpie#3213 — Qoder per-model queue 503 rests the whole account
- yetone/magpie#4049 — `x-magpie-fallback` behavior; a non-last candidate gives way immediately
- yetone/magpie#4998 — request for an answer timeout so queue/reasoning activity cannot block failover

I searched existing issues and did not find one specifically asking to make the Qoder queue budget configurable or to align it with Qoder's 1-hour client. If the 4-minute cap is deliberate, please document the recommended Codex workaround and consider exposing the setting anyway.

issue.title: model test: 28 probes all answered 503 in the same second, yet the panel says "all 7 models available"

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

The provider editor says **"7 个模型全部可用" (all 7 models available)** with a green dot on every model, while the same test round produced **28 × HTTP 503** in `usage.jsonl` in the same second. A user cannot tell from the UI that the provider is in fact serving nothing.

This is the presentation side of the queue-refusal problem already diagnosed in #3213 (Qoder's per-model queue 503 is classified as `failOther`, so `restKey()` rests the whole account). That issue is about routing behaviour. This one is about the **test result being reported as success**.

## Build

- magpie `0.1.3970`, macOS (arm64), gateway 127.0.0.1:3425
- provider: `qoder` (accounts `2048416010@qq.com`, `1156269458@qq.com`) and `qoder-cn` (3 accounts), plan `personal_standard`
- credits are not exhausted (qoder 379/1500 and 812/1300; qoder-cn 1424/2200, 1200/2000, 1200/2000), tokens are valid (earliest expiry 23h out), and `openapi.qoder.sh` / `openapi.qoder.com.cn` both answer 401 — so this is not quota, sign-in, or reachability

## What the panel showed

Pressing 测试模型 on `qoder` with all 7 models selected, the footer read `7 个模型全部可用` and every model carried a green dot: Ultimate, Fast, Cantus, Qwen4-Max, Qwen3.8-Flash, Kimi-K3.1-Pro, DeepSeek-Flash. The list header read `供应商列表 · 刚刚`, so this was a fresh run, not a cached card.

## What the same run actually recorded

`~/.config/magpie/usage.jsonl`, `kind: provider_test`, `source: probe`, all within one second:

```
13:15:40.886  qoder/ultimate        503   157 ms
13:15:40.886  qoder/fast            503
13:15:40.886  qoder/cmodel          503
13:15:40.886  qoder/qmodel_latest   503
13:15:40.886  qoder/qfmodel         503
13:15:41.339  qoder/kmodel_latest   503
13:15:41.347  qoder/dfmodel         503
... three more rounds of the same 7 up to 13:15:46 — 28 records, 28 × 503
```

Every probe failed, every model showed green.

## The upstream answer it was hiding

`~/.config/magpie/routing/2026-11-16.jsonl`:

```json
{"id": "qoder", "model": "ultimate", "status": 503, "ms": 157, "sentBy": "plugin",
 "fail": "other",
 "error": "Qoder: Qoder queued the request for ultimate (this plan's queue: p4, 1 ahead); try again in 60s",
 "rest": {"why": "other", "until": "2026-11-16T13:26:04+08:00", "by": "backoff",
          "failures": 17, "key": "qoder@2048416010@qq.com"}}
```
